name: Earth Sound Research
notes: American amplifier/effects company founded in Farmingdale, NY in 1971. Rare Graphic Fuzz makes it a significant historical dirt-pedal maker despite a tiny effects catalog.

name: EarthTone
dirt_evidence: Apple Fuzz; Fuzz Mix; Pepper Fuzz; Pepper Fuzz White; Orange Drive; Voice Drive
notes: Effects Database indexes 14 products, including multiple fuzz/drive models. Pepper Fuzz examples are explicitly documented as made in Italy.

name: Chicago Stompworks

notes: Mike Po's Chicago builder. Effects Database says he also previously made pedals as Podals and custom pedals as Van Houten Custom Shop. Preserve those aliases/roles for reconciliation.

name: Pepper Electronics / Pepper Pedals

name: RGW Electronics
dirt_evidence: Bad Bob Booster; Dirty Dan; Lightnin' Luke; Mojo Face; Pistol Pete; Smokin Sam
notes: Six-product historical Effects Database catalog with multiple dirt-oriented models. Full builder history and production dates require Queue B research.

name: MadeByMike
notes: Small British builder captured in Effects Database's Distortion+ related-model tree. Preserve as a micro-builder rather than losing it among one-product pages.

name: On Off Effects
notes: Effects Database documents a dedicated distortion pedal. Geography and broader catalog remain to be established.

name: Big Knob Pedals
notes: Hand-wired DOD 250-derived overdrive. Effects Database places it in the DOD 250 lineage tree, giving it strong dirt relevance.

name: Wiz Pedal
dirt_evidence: Model A; Model D; Mini-D; other D-style overdrive products
notes: Hand-made US overdrive builder with multiple D-style models and compact variants. Product-level generation mapping can wait for Queue B.

name: Cause & Effect Pedals
notes: Ontario boutique builder, previously captured here for its 2009 FET Dream. Retained in this tranche only as a lineage cross-check, not a new entity.

name: General Guitar Gadgets

notes: Important DIY kit ecosystem rather than a conventional pedal factory. Keep separate from assembled commercial builders and preserve its role in historical DIY access.
